verses.text: Then Job answered:
"How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
You've insulted me ten times and aren't ashamed to keep attacking me.
If I really have gone wrong, my mistake is mine to bear.
If you're going to set yourselves above me and use my disgrace as evidence against me,
know this: God has wronged me and caught me in his net.
I cry out, 'I've been wronged!' but nobody hears me. I call for help and get no justice.
He's put a wall across my way so I can't get through and covered my paths with darkness.
He's stripped me of my honor and taken the crown off my head.
He's torn me down on every side until I'm finished. He's pulled up my hope like a tree.
He's kindled his anger against me and counts me as one of his enemies.
His troops come together, build a siege ramp against me, and camp around my tent.
He's driven my brothers far from me. The people who know me have become strangers.
My relatives have gone away, and my close friends have forgotten me.
The people staying in my house and my servant women treat me as a stranger. To them I'm an outsider.
I call my servant, but he doesn't answer, even when I beg him myself.
My breath offends my wife, and my own mother's children can't stand me.
Even little children despise me. When I stand up, they speak against me.
My closest friends are repulsed by me. The people I loved have turned against me.
My bones cling to my skin and flesh. I've escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Have pity on me, my friends. Have pity, because God's hand has struck me.
Why do you hound me as God does? Haven't you had enough of tearing at my flesh?
If only my words were written down! If only they were recorded in a book!
If only they were cut into rock forever with an iron tool and filled with lead!
But I know my Redeemer lives. In the end he'll stand upon the earth.
After my skin has been destroyed, I'll see God in my flesh.
I'll see him myself, on my side. My own eyes will see him. I won't be a stranger to him. My heart is spent within me.
If you say, 'How can we keep hounding him?' because you think the root of the problem is in me,
you should fear the sword. Anger brings the punishment of the sword, so you'll know there is a judgment."
